html:
From the 1950s American companies built tuna canneries on the harbour at Pago Pago, which became the largest private employers in American Samoa. Fishing fleets landed their catch there and the cans went to the United States market.

The plants grew because goods from the territory could enter the US free of duty, and because local wage rules differed from the mainland. Many workers came from independent Samoa next door.

The industry made the territory depend on one product. When US minimum wages rose and one plant closed in 2009, the same year as the tsunami, thousands of jobs went at once.
